subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw core expose persisted per-cron lifecycle hooks that can run shell commands or webhook actions, and what trust boundary/API should own that behavior?
rationale: The remaining work changes public cron schema and can execute unattended local commands or outbound network calls, so automation should not choose the product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow core hook API
options.body: Define an additive cron hook/gate contract with security-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

options.title: Keep hooks external
options.body: Declare command cron plus plugin hooks as the supported boundary and document the plugin/ClawHub pattern instead of adding CronJob.hooks to core.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave this as an acknowledged product gap until maintainers are ready to own the security model and public API surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core hook API
recommendation.body: Define an additive cron hook/gate contract with security-reviewed command/webhook permissions, runtime phases, failure semantics, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on the cron schema/runtime surfaces and authored the most specific prior routing review for this issue.
